analysis:
Reviewed the work-disk (--disk) additions to the sandbox CLI, relevant to TB-013, T-061 and A-019.

SandboxInstaller.swift (head 11-12, 29-31, 103-111, 133-137): disks are appended as separate argv elements ([--disk, path]) to the /bin/sh installer call, with no shell string interpolation. Option support is still detected by substring search of the downloaded script (supportsDisks, line 107), as for --plan and --json-progress. The installer remains the trust anchor (T-061). HTTPS-only download, redirect, size and shebang checks are unchanged (lines 46-101).

SandboxSetupCommand.swift:
- validate rejects empty --disk values. Options map disks through SandboxWorkDisk.absolutePath, which is not supplied.
- withInstaller refuses --disk when the script does not name it (head ~480-485).
- checkWorkDisks runs before install. When ownership is off, and only if not --yes and stdin is a TTY, it asks for confirmation and then calls enableOwnership(mount). That runs `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` on the mount point from the user path or from workDiskCandidates.
- chooseWorkDisk lists candidate volumes interactively.
- requestAddonPlan now prints the installer's last 5 stderr lines when the plan fails with disks. That is the same trust level as the installer output already rendered.

No concrete regression was found in the visible code.

Unverified contracts for integration or deeper review (SandboxWorkDisk.swift was not supplied):
1. enableOwnership must invoke sudo/diskutil with an argv array, not a shell string. Mount points and volume names are attacker-influenceable via the volume label of an inserted drive. It must also pass a validated mount point, with no option-injection (for example, a leading '-').
2. absolutePath and volume(at:) need symlink/TOCTOU handling, since the path is checked and then handed to the installer.
3. candidates() should filter on APFS, external and ownership state.

Threat-model gap to consider: TB-013/A-019 currently describe the CLI running code only as the owner. This PR adds an interactive sudo elevation (diskutil enableOwnership) and VM images/jobs on external, unattested volumes. T-041's note on external volumes covers only the KV cache, not the sandbox work disks. TB-013 should document both, even though no exploitable flaw is visible here.
